claims.statement: The eFTI Regulation creates a common framework for machine-readable freight information and certified service providers.
The e-CMR framework supports electronic consignment notes used for commercial transport-contract evidence.

contrary_evidence: Neither eFTI nor e-CMR creates a detention entitlement; the underlying contract and factual causation remain decisive.

structure.control_point: The tamper-evident dwell-time evidence packet and matched settlement receipt
structure.critical_dependency: Contractual detention entitlement and trusted timestamps accepted by shippers or their dispute process

thesis: For road carriers and freight factors, bind e-CMR or eFTI shipment records, geofenced arrival and departure, dock acknowledgements and the transport contract into a detention claim. Track the claim through credit note or cash receipt and charge only on settlement. TMS vendors, factoring firms and carrier associations offer one-to-many distribution; verified resolutions build lane, shipper and evidence-sufficiency benchmarks rather than a generic fleet dashboard.
title: Freight Detention Evidence Settlement
